say: Today we learn variables. A variable is a name that stores a value. Think of a labeled box: the label is the name, and the thing inside is the value.
board: Variable = a name that stores a value

say: Look at this line: score = 10. It puts the value 10 into the variable called score.
board:
Variable = a name that stores a value
score = 10

say: Careful: the = sign here does not mean equal like in math. It means assign: compute the right side, then store it in the name on the left.
board:
Variable = a name that stores a value
score = 10
= means assign (put into), NOT equal

say: That is why score = score + 1 is allowed. Python computes the right side first: 10 + 1 is 11. Then it stores 11 back into score. So a variable's value can change.
board:
Variable = a name that stores a value
score = 10
= means assign (put into), NOT equal
score = score + 1  -> score is now 11
A variable's value can change

say: Names are case-sensitive. score with a small s and Score with a capital S are two different variables. Capital letters matter.
board:
Variable = a name that stores a value
score = 10
= means assign (put into), NOT equal
score = score + 1  -> score is now 11
A variable's value can change
score and Score are DIFFERENT variables (case-sensitive)

say: Every value has a type. A whole number like 42 has the type int, short for integer. Text in quotes like "hello" has the type str, short for string.
board:

A variable's value can change
score and Score are DIFFERENT variables (case-sensitive)
42 is an int (whole number)
"hello" is a str (text)

say: So variables do not only hold numbers. name = "Maya" stores the text Maya in a variable called name. And the computer does not understand what a name means: a variable called price can hold anything.

"hello" is a str (text)
name = "Maya" stores the text Maya in name

say: Summary: a variable is a name that stores a value. = assigns, it is not equal. The value can change. Names are case-sensitive. Values have types: int for whole numbers, str for text.
